description: Per-drug lipophilicity and ionisation for the P29.2 well-stirred CL arm's microsomal-binding (fu_mic) correction (P29.6). logP is ChEMBL_37 ALOGP (ChemAxon-computed, spot-checked against the EBI molecule API). pKa and ionisation class are the most-basic (or strongest-acidic) measured pKa with a per-drug source; they set the ionisation class only. Every drug here is a base or a neutral at pH 7.4, so the Austin/Hallifax-Houston equation uses logP for all of them (logD7.4 is reserved for acids, of which there are none). No drug-specific number is fitted.

fu_mic.equation: Hallifax-Houston 2006: fu_mic = 1 / (1 + C * 10^(0.072*L^2 + 0.067*L - 1.126)), L = logP for bases/neutrals and logD7.4 for acids, C = microsomal protein concentration (mg/mL). Reduces to the Austin 2002 relationship's reference at C = 1 mg/mL.
fu_mic.equation_pmids_note: 12433825 (Austin 2002) and 16552024 (Hallifax & Houston 2006) are method/equation citations, not per-drug records, so they name the fu_mic relationship rather than any one drug; both verified against PubMed.
fu_mic.protein_mg_ml_note: The benchmark CLint rows (ChEMBL activity comments) record substrate concentration ranges, not microsomal protein concentration, so no per-assay C is available. We declare C = 1 mg/mL: Austin et al. 2002 (PMID 12433825) derived the lipophilicity relationship from rat-liver-microsome binding measured at 0.25, 1 and 4 mg/mL and expressed it per mg/mL, and 1 mg/mL is a standard human-liver-microsome CLint incubation concentration. This default is declared, not tuned: the train result beats the mean baseline at both 0.5 and 1 mg/mL.
